scope: Linux and macOS native calendar initialization in process local_time and schema creation_date
replacement: Shared private safe initializer: explicit zero numeric fields and null zone on Linux; libc 0.2.190 generated safe field defaults on macOS.
dependency_evidence: Pinned libc 0.2.190 declares Linux tm in s! without Default. Apple tm is exhaustive in s2!, which generates field defaults; tm_zone uses custom_default(ptr::null_mut()). No dependency changes.
compatibility: All ten numeric fields remain zero and tm_zone remains null before the existing native calls. Time source, localtime_r invocation, failure handling and output conversion remain unchanged. No toolkit API or trait bounds change.
exclusions: Other Unix targets retain the existing zeroed initialization pending platform-specific verification. Windows is unchanged. Native time/localtime_r calls remain under investigation; this does not establish a permanent system exception.
inventory: Removes two executed unsafe initialization operations on Linux/macOS. The process zeroed block remains lexically present only for other Unix cfgs; schema initialization shared a block with FFI. Source counts therefore stay unchanged. Supported Unix compiler diagnostics should lose the process initialization block once per compilation unit; exact counts still require capture.
local_verification: Linux x86_64 empty_calendar field-value regression passed
